gh pr create --repo scottdensmore/Cakebrew --base main --head fix/pin-nil-block-crash \
  --title "Fix EXC_BAD_ACCESS when invoking brew with a nil return block" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## The crash
Clicking **Pin Formula** crashed with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS`. `pinSelectedFormula:` calls `pinFormula:withReturnBlock:` with a **nil** block, but `performAsyncBrewCommandWithArguments:` invoked that block **unconditionally** — at the DEBUG warning (which fires *before* the task even runs) and again at the task-done message. Calling a `NULL` block is an `EXC_BAD_ACCESS`.

Every prior caller (install/uninstall/tap/untap/upgrade) always passed a non-nil block (they stream output to a window), so this latent bug only surfaced once pin/unpin ([#41](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/pull/41)) legitimately passed `nil`.

## Fix
- Route both interface block invocations through a new nil-guarding helper `invokeOutputBlock:withString:`.
- Also guard `BPTask`'s streaming callback (`self.updateBlock`) — normally gated by `shouldUsePartialUpdates`, but a nil could still race in if `cleanup` clears `updateBlock` while a dispatched output block is pending.

## Test
The crash path needs a real `brew` subprocess **and** the mock overrides pin/unpin — so neither the hermetic unit suite nor the mock-based UI tests would catch a recurrence. I extracted the helper specifically so the nil-safety is unit-testable directly: `invokeOutputBlock:` with a nil block must be a safe no-op (**without the guard this crashes the whole test process**) and still delivers the string to a non-nil block.

## Verification
- ✅ Debug build (the config that crashed), **0 warnings**
- ✅ **59 unit tests green** (57 + 2 nil-safety regression tests)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
Fixed and merged — [PR #42](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/pull/42), `main` at `54698d1`.

## Root cause
`pinSelectedFormula:` calls `pinFormula:withReturnBlock:` with a **nil** block (pin has no output to stream). But `performAsyncBrewCommandWithArguments:` invoked that block **unconditionally** — first at the DEBUG warning (which fires *before* the task even runs, so you crashed the instant you clicked Pin), then again at the task-done message. Calling a `NULL` block is `EXC_BAD_ACCESS`. It was a latent bug: every previous caller always passed a non-nil block, so pin/unpin were the first to expose it.

## The fix
- Both interface block-calls now route through a nil-guarding helper `invokeOutputBlock:withString:`.
- Also guarded `BPTask`'s streaming callback against a nil-block race during cleanup.
- **Regression test:** the crash needs a real `brew` subprocess *and* the mock overrides pin/unpin — so nothing automated would have caught a recurrence. I extracted the helper specifically to make the nil-safety unit-testable: `invokeOutputBlock:` with a nil block must be a safe no-op (without the guard, that test crashes the whole process) and still delivers to a non-nil block.

**Verified:** Debug build (your config) 0 warnings, 59 unit tests green, CI green (the one UI failure was an unrelated flake in `testTapPresentsInputDialog` — the Tap button was slow to appear; a re-run passed clean).

**Please pull `main`, rebuild, and re-test the Pin click** — the full flow should now work: pinning runs `brew pin`, then the list refreshes. One thing you'll notice: the selection resets after pinning (same as it does after install/uninstall), so re-select the formula to see the menu flip to an enabled "Unpin Formula." The persistent **detail-pane pin indicator** in the next PR (PR 3) will make that state obvious at a glance.

Sorry that one slipped through — the gap was that pin/unpin are the only nil-block callers, and both the hermetic units and the mock-based UI tests structurally can't exercise the real command path. The new test closes that gap.
